reason: Fire is the obvious source of light for the sheltered cave.
expectation: Fire will light the cave's interior for painting.

effect: The fire lit the cave wall, revealing the goal of painting an animal from memory.
reaction: The lit wall makes the next task clear.
reason: Weathered rock can contain pigments, and water may help turn them into paint.
expectation: The rock and water will produce a usable pigment or paint.

effect: The weathered rock and water made pigment suitable for marking the cave wall.
reaction: The pigment preparation makes physical sense.
reason: The pigment can be applied to the lit cave wall to begin the painting.
expectation: The pigment will make a painted mark or picture on the wall.

effect: Pigment and memory produced an animal painting; the next goal is to add stars.
reaction: The automatic use of memory neatly completed the picture.
reason: Stars are available and the new goal explicitly asks for them in the painting.
expectation: Stars will be added to the cave painting.

effect: The painting now includes stars, completing that goal; making a song remains.
reaction: The animal and stars now share the wall.
reason: A call is a plausible starting point for making a song, so I will check its available partners.
expectation: The inspection should reveal what can be combined with the call to make a song.

effect: Inspecting Call automatically used the cave to produce an echo, suggesting a sound-based route to the song.
reaction: The reflected call is a surprising starting point for music.
reason: I will check what the echo can be combined with, since its role in making a song is not yet clear.
expectation: The inspection will reveal a useful partner for the echo, possibly leading toward a song.

effect: Echo and Memory automatically produced a song, revealing the goal of passing on community knowledge.
reaction: Remembering and repeating sounds makes a plausible route to a song.
reason: The song can carry the community's shared discovery to others.
expectation: The community will use the song to pass on what it has learned.

effect: Song has no available combination, so it does not directly carry the shared discovery.
reaction: That was an unexpected dead end.
reason: Shared discovery is the clearest remaining lead for passing on knowledge; checking its partners avoids another unsupported guess.
expectation: The inspection will reveal how the discovery can be passed on.

effect: Inspecting Shared discovery revealed Story as its sole partner and automatically produced Teaching, completing the final goal.
reaction: The emphasis on explaining evidence and practising skills made the ending satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making Teaching was most worthwhile: it connected sharing a discovery with explaining how it was tested and letting others practise skills.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying Song with Shared discovery was a dead end; the result gave no indication of what to try with Song.

surprise.text: I was surprised that a call echoing in the cave led to a song through memory and repetition.

arbitrary.text: The echo-to-song connection was not obvious to me beforehand, though the explanation made it plausible afterward.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see more combinations that connect physical processes with learning and creative expression, as the pigment and echo sequences did.
